cells.tense: You are keeping the shape of this right now, hand on it.
cells.ask: Build one thing that holds for someone else, mostly on your own, and leave it up all week without checking it.
cells.core:
Hard conditions have been on you, and you're in it — standing, not braced. You're not shoving the structure around; you're the one keeping it up, and it holds because you're in it.

There's a part already strong here: what you carry, you carry alone, no one watching. That part is working. The next thing it can feed is what you hope for. Pick one structure that needs your strength to stay up and that you'd also want anyway, and let keeping it up be based on wanting it, not just because it's there. Setting the pattern is what you do. Setting it toward something you hope for is what keeps it there.
cells.sheetLine: You carry it yourself, and it holds because you're in it.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get established

cells.tense: You are bracing the structure against a future that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you hold up for someone else that they could hold themselves, and let it drop for a day.
cells.core:
You're miles ahead of where anyone else is, building the structure for conditions that haven't hit. You keep tightening the rules, checking the pattern, getting the form right before it's needed — and it's draining you rather than steadying you. Something that used to be about keeping things upright is now about controlling what's coming, and the grip keeps you from resting.

That's not more strength; that's the exchange part. Give and take in even balance, without keeping score. Let one structure you didn't agree to run stay unheld today: don't reinforce it, don't tidy it. See what happens when it stands on its own. If it's up without you, you'll know what was actually yours to carry.
cells.sheetLine: You're tightening what hasn't even moved yet.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get established

cells.tense: You stopped at a doorway, and the doorway is already behind you.
cells.ask: Tell one person one specific hard thing you've carried without complaint, and let them simply know it.
cells.core:
There was a room where you held up the structure and nobody clocked it. You're still at that doorway, not quite back in the present, not quite away from it. The strength to persist is there; you're not drawing on it yet today.

More endurance won't touch this. What's needed is the acknowledgement, the outside witness. Get that lifted, and then you can release what's already complete. One person, one thing you carried on your own: just say it. You don't have to ask them for anything. That's the charge that comes back into the starved part — not more pressure, but the straight honor your private persistence didn't get.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at a door and the door is behind you.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get established

cells.tense: You're keeping the structure up while saying it runs itself.
cells.ask: Name one piece of structure you set up and currently call just the way things run.
cells.core:
You're already keeping the form up — the rules, the order, the way things run here. You set half of that up yourself, but you describe it like it was there before you. Your persistence is doing the work; you haven't said it's yours.

There's a simpler angle. What the structure lets you do is keep going toward something you hope for, not just hold the walls up. When you start naming what's yours, that keeping-up stops being invisible. One piece, said out loud, called what it is. This is the earlier form of the same line: from a structure that apparently runs itself to the one person who decided how it runs. Your persistence is the reason it holds. Start there.
cells.sheetLine: You built the structure and call it just how things are.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get established
